caption: Kar. 32. Altar (Kar. Cem., Pl. 16, No. 7092)
labels: sic, over the y of soreyi, by line 2
reading: (1)wosi : sore(2)y?i : mli(3)tẖideqowi : teme(4)ykdiye : tedḫelowi : (5)ẖ?[.][.][.][.][.][.][.][.][.][.][.][.] (6)terikelo(7)wi : slẖsmnp(8)t : semlo(9)wi :
notes: Four rows, each read right to left; row 1 holds lines 1-3, row 2 line 4, row 3 lines 5-7, row 4 lines 8-9. Line 2 'y?': Griffith marks the sign 'sic'; it is drawn as an H-like y joined to i. Line 2/3 name: first sign a 3 with short tail (m, possibly ẖ); 'ẖ?' after t is a 3 with a long tail to the lower left; 'e?' before qowi is a large flat-topped 5-shape (e or l); 'qo' = slash+3 then slash (could be s+o+o or ẖ+o+o). Line 4 'se?' is a J with hatched strokes (damaged se); 'kai': Z-topped 3 with long tail (k), then a 4 overlapping an S2 group read a+i (could be e+k). Line 5: one 3 with a long tail running left (ẖ?) then a long hatched stretch, about 12 sign widths, counted as 12 [.] (estimate). Line 7/8 group: five 3-shaped/hook signs before n (ʌ with long tail) and p (ξ with long tail); the m/ẖ assignments are by tail length only. 'l?' after p is a small flat-topped hook. Line numbers 7 and 9 stand over the w of -owi.
check_notes: All 13 entries placed. Name A = mli + tẖideqowi (names table, Index A/B/C mli); the sign after t is ẖ in the type (rounded 3 with descender, unlike the flat m of mli), so the Index C typing 'mlitmideqowi' is a typing error. Mother = temeykdiye (names B, Index C): the copy's J with hatching is m (same J form as m in semlowi), and its 5+Z group is d. Father: Griffith prints empty brackets; the copy's single 3 before the hatched stretch is kept as ẖ? and the 12 [.] are kept. Description slẖs mnpt : semlowi (Index A/B/C) fixes the row of 3-shaped signs: s l ẖ s m n p t; the hook after p is t. The type has a space after slẖs; the copy shows none, so none is added.

caption: Kar. 33. Altar
reading: (1)wosi sore(2)yi : tbi(3)yeqowi : ato : mẖe : psoẖ(4)te : at : mẖe : psḫ(5)rkete : ḫmlol ẖolke(6)tese
notes: Three rows: row 1 lines 1-3, row 2 (right group then left group) lines 3-5, row 3 lines 5-6. No divider between wosi and sore (clear gap). 'e' before qowi is a large flat-topped 5-shape (e or l); 'qo' as in Kar. 32. 'ato': a = 5 and Z with long tail drawn apart; to = ب with dot below. 'l?' between mẖe and p in the first formula is a small upright hook, possibly a divider or i. 'k?' in psok?te is a bold 3 with heavy top, no long tail (k or ḫ). In 'at : mẖe' the t is a 5-shape with a dot. Row 3 'q' = slash+3 (could be o+s).
check_notes: All 10 entries placed. Name tbiyeqowi agrees. Formula A (ato : mẖe : psoẖte): the small upright mark read l? in step 1 stands where the type has a divider, and is written as one; the bold 3 read k? is ẖ. Formula B agrees. Formula C (ḫmlol ẖolketese): the copy's slash+3 is ẖ+o (not q) and its 9+Z group is k+e (not a), the known traps; the space after ḫmlol follows the type and a visible gap in the copy. Index C 'mḫe' is the general headword (normalised ḫ); this text's own formula-B table entry reads mẖe, as the copy does.

caption: Kar. 34. Altar
labels: ? (Griffith's own query, printed in the line) after p, by line 13
? (Griffith's own query, raised) over the second hatched sign, by line 13
reading: (1)wos?i : (2)asoreyi (3)yilili kete lowi : a(4)tmso : nẖsnye : te(5)rikelowi : ḫr? : tedḫe?lo(6)wi son(7)i[.][.][.][.][.](8)towi slẖ(9)mn[.][.][.][.][.][.]towi : ato mẖe : (10)pi?soẖte : at m(11)ḫepsi ḫrkete (12)ḫmlole (13)pẖo[.][.][.]
notes: Six rows; most rows have a right and a left group, read right to left. 's?' in wosi is a thin 3 crossed by a stroke. '(2)a': the 2 stands over the 2 of the a-group. 'yilili': 4 crossed by three slashes (y+i), then two 4+hook groups read l+i each (could be te). In this copy the S-shape stands where -lowi/tedḫelowi need l, so it is read l? there; elsewhere S is e. Row 2 'a' at start could be k+e (Z with long tail + S); 'mẖo' could be m+q. Row 3 'r?' is a dotted (damaged) ω; the hatched sign after tedḫ is read e?. Row 4 right group: q (slash+3), n, (7), i, one hatched sign [.], four dots [.]x4, then a ب-like sign without dot read to?. Row 4 left group: hatched 3 (s?), S, 3 with tail, 7-shaped sign crossing the tail of n (9), five dots trailing under the line plus one hatched sign (6 [.]), then an L+loop sign read to?, a dotted ) read m?, a bold 4 read i?. Row 5 formula A: p? is a bold Z/ξ with long base (10), then a hatched sign [.], 3+slash read s+o (or q), 3 with long tail ẖ?, te. Formula B has ḫ drawn as ⊏ in mḫe (11) and p as zigzag Σ with long tail. Row 6: '(12)ḫml?ol?' then a small raised 5-shape (l?), then (13) a Σ with long base read p?, Griffith's printed ?, a slash o?, and three hatched signs (an n-like sign with a box below, two H-like signs) read n? i? i?.
check_notes: 29 of 30 entries placed; the Index B entry for Kar. 60 (cf. Kar. 34 C) is compare-only. Name A yililiketelowi (names table, Index C; yi also indexed as a title): the copy's 5+2 group is k+e and its S before owi is l. In this copy S serves for l in -lowi (confirmed by the name), so the S of tedḫelowi is read l too (rule 4). Title of C 'at mso' (Index A, C): the 3 is s. Father nẖsnye and mother ḫr(?) agree (Griffith's query kept as r?). Description 1 'soni mnitowi' (Griffith marks the reference to Kar. 34 with (?)): copy so+n+i then one hatched sign and four dots ([.]x5, kept) then to w i; the type's m n i fall in the lost stretch. Description 2 'slẖ : mnptowi': the copy has no divider after slẖ and shows six lost signs where the type has only p; kept as the copy shows. Formula A pisoẖte: the hatched sign after p is i. Formula C 'ḫmlole pẖo....': the mark after p that looked like a printed ? in the copy is taken as the damaged ẖ the type shows; the copy's three hatched, unread signs are written [.][.][.] (the type has four dots). The labels field still records that ? mark as seen in step 1.

caption: Kar. 35. Stela
notes: Row 1 (right only) has no printed line number. Row 2 holds the rest: right group, middle group, left group. 'qo' = 3 with slash then slash (could be s+y). 'ẖ?' is a small 3 with long tail to lower left; d is a rising stroke with a hook. 'e?' before m is a small S. 'se?' is a bold ᴗ with two lightly hatched slashes. 'ni?': a 4 crossed by a rising stroke ending in a Z (n+i, could be a). k is a Z-topped 3 whose tail runs far right under the following signs. Left group: the first sign (s?) is a 3 with hatching strokes trailing under the line toward the divider; no lost sign counted there. 'di' = 4 sharing its bar with a rising hooked stroke (d).
check_notes: All 7 entries placed. Three names (names table A, persons 1-3; Index C). Person 1 (qo)mdeyeqewi: the 3 with long tail after qo is m; the 7-shape with a slash before it, read m+o in step 1, is one q (one slash only, as the type). Person 2 weredikeyeqewi: the bold ᴗ with hatched strokes is r, the rising hooked stroke is d, the small S before q is e; Index C's 'qoewi' typing is wrong (one slash: qe-wi). Person 3 k(?)dilqo: the hatched 3 is k (Griffith's own query kept as k?), the S is l. Index C qo ('introducing name') is the qo before person 1.
